Davenport's rules for your trees

Local measurements and geology — not national boilerplate.

8 ftclearance required over Davenport sidewalks
14 ftclearance required over streets and alleys
3–5 yrstypical pruning cycle for mature shade trees
Winterthe only season to prune oaks in Iowa (oak wilt)

Davenport's tree ordinance puts specific numbers on private trees: branches must be pruned to 8 feet of clearance over sidewalks and 14 feet over streets and alleys, must not obstruct street lights, traffic signs, or intersection sight lines — and if your tree encroaching on the right-of-way damages a vehicle, the ordinance can make you liable. City-side trees are the mirror image: nothing in the right-of-way gets cut without the city arborist's authorization. The practical read: keep your trees clear of the listed heights, and call Public Works (563.326.7923) before touching anything between the sidewalk and the curb.

Sources: City of Davenport Tree Ordinance (Ordinance 8.14.280 and Art. IV, ecode360); City of Davenport Public Works

Pruning for storms, not for looks

Good pruning in this climate is structural: removing deadwood before the wind does, thinning where the canopy is too dense to spill gusts, and correcting co-dominant stems — the twin-leader shape with a weak V-crotch that splits in storms. That last one is the signature failure of the silver maples all over Davenport's older neighborhoods. What good pruning is not: topping. Lopping the canopy flat forces weakly-attached regrowth that is more storm-prone than what was removed, and no reputable crew does it.

Timing matters more in IA than people think. Most species take pruning best in the dormant season, when structure is visible and disease pressure is low. The exception that matters here is oak: Iowa State University Extension advises pruning oaks only in the dormant winter months, because the sap-feeding beetles that spread oak wilt — a fatal, untreatable disease — are active through the growing season and are drawn to fresh cuts.

  • Sidewalk and street clearance cuts to city-code heights
  • Deadwood and hanger removal — the cheap version of storm prep
  • Structural pruning on young trees, so they never need cabling later
  • No topping — ever

Davenport Tree Trimming & Pruning — FAQ

Whose job is the tree between the sidewalk and the street?
In Davenport, the parking-strip tree is generally a city right-of-way tree: you cannot remove or trim it without city-arborist authorization — but the ordinance still requires you, the adjacent owner, to keep it pruned to clearance heights over the sidewalk. When a right-of-way tree needs real work, start with Public Works at 563.326.7923.
How often should mature trees be pruned?
A mature shade tree in good shape typically wants attention every 3–5 years — deadwood out, clearance maintained, structure checked. Fast-growing soft species like silver maple sit at the short end of that range; slow growers like oak at the long end. Annual pruning of a mature tree is a sales program, not arboriculture.
When should oaks NOT be pruned?
From roughly March through October — the growing season — pruning oaks risks oak wilt, a fatal fungal disease spread by sap beetles drawn to fresh cuts. Iowa State University Extension guidance is to prune oaks during winter dormancy. If an oak limb must come off in summer (storm damage), the cut should be sealed immediately — the one case where pruning paint is actually recommended.
Can pruning really reduce storm damage?
Substantially. Most storm failures start at predictable defects — deadwood, cracked limbs, dense sail-like canopies, and V-crotches — all of which pruning addresses. It converts the question from 'what will the next derecho take' to 'what did we already remove on purpose.'
